text:
Connor O'Brien: heads up — need rollout plan for the incident-bot status-page changes (phase prompts + draft-sync). want to do this w/ feature flags + canary in one region first. can folks confirm what we’re thinking + any gotchas?

Devon Price: yup. PRs in flight are:
- pr_312: phase-based prompts + enforce next-update time
- pr_317: draft-sync on incident state transitions
both behind flags right now.

Dylan Brooks: +1. i’d like to keep the blast radius tiny. canary should be a single oncall rotation + single hosted region if possible.

Connor O'Brien: what’s the smallest meaningful canary? bot is global in Slack, but the status component / incident routing can be scoped.

Miles Thornton: we can scope by “incident namespace” and region label in the incident metadata. incident-bot already gets `service` + `region` from the incident create flow.
proposal:
- enable flags only when `region in {us-west}` AND `incident.severity >= 1`
- everything else behaves like today (manual status updates)

Rafael Mendes: us-west is ok as canary but i’d rather pick a region w/ stable oncall coverage (fewer vacation gaps). us-east is busier.

Christine Wong: status page component work is landing w/ region breakdown: us-east/us-west/eu-west. so canary in *us-west* maps cleanly and we’ll see if the component selection UX makes sense.

Connor O'Brien: ok. what are the flags called right now?

Devon Price: current config has:
- `status_update_prompts_v1`
- `status_page_draft_sync_v1`
both default false.
there’s also a per-incident override param in `/incident settings` but it’s admin-only.

Sara Al-Masri: do we want a “kill switch” that doesn’t require redeploy? e.g. remote config / configmap reload.

Devon Price: it’s remote config (launchdarkly-style) in `incident-bot-config`, can toggle w/o deploy. i can add a separate emergency kill `status_page_sync_disable_all` if we want belt+suspenders.

Dylan Brooks: yes please on the explicit kill switch. also: can we ensure the sync writes *draft* only, not publish, in the canary phase?

Devon Price: already the behavior:
- on state transition, bot creates a *draft* update w/ the template + prefilled fields
- oncall has to click “Publish” in the bot modal
no auto-publish.

Rafael Mendes: good. what about preventing low-info updates? i don’t want this to increase spam on status.

Miles Thornton: pr_312 adds guardrails: it blocks publish if the update is empty. it requires at least one of impact/mitigation/next-update time. (we can tune but that’s the default)

Aisha Bello: for canary success metrics: i can put dashboards on (a) time-to-first-update, (b) % updates missing “next update time”, (c) # of status updates per incident. we should set a baseline from last 30d.

Connor O'Brien: nice. release timing: i’m aiming Tuesday 10am PT for deploy + flags off, then turn on canary after deploy.

Christine Wong: request: please don’t enable canary until after we merge the status component mapping changes for us-west. otherwise bot prompts may reference components not yet visible.

Devon Price: ack. dependency is `status-components-us-west` config landing. i can check with Nora but i think it’s already in staging.

Connor O'Brien: can we make the canary enablement a checklist item w/ explicit sign-off from SRE + status page owner?

Rafael Mendes: yes. i’ll be on point for SRE signoff.

Dylan Brooks: canary duration? i’d prefer 1 week or at least 3-5 incidents, whichever is longer.

Miles Thornton: agree. and we should include at least one long-running degradation scenario (not just a clean sev2 blip) to test the “next update” enforcement.

Sara Al-Masri: rollout steps draft:
1) Deploy incident-bot w/ pr_312 + pr_317 merged (flags default off)
2) Verify in staging: state transition creates draft, prompts show correct template phase
3) Enable `status_update_prompts_v1` for `region=us-west`, `sev>=1`
4) After 24h, enable `status_page_draft_sync_v1` for same scope
5) Monitor dashboards + #incidents channel feedback
6) If issues, flip kill switch + revert flags

Connor O'Brien: i like the staggered enablement (prompts first, then sync). Devon, can we implement the scope rule in remote config cleanly?

Devon Price: yes, remote config supports targeting rules. i’ll add conditions for `incident.region` and `incident.severity`. for region, it’s `us-west` today, not `us-west-1` (double-check).

Christine Wong: region string should be `us-west` in incident annotations; control plane emits that.

Rafael Mendes: question: if an incident starts in us-west but later we realize it’s cross-region, do we update scope? i don’t want bot blocking updates.

Miles Thornton: scope is evaluated per action. if you change incident metadata to add `regions=[us-west,us-east]` it’ll still match rule (contains us-west) unless we make it “only us-west”. recommend “contains us-west” to keep behavior consistent.

Dylan Brooks: but that might expand blast radius if incident is global and we still want to canary? hmm.

Connor O'Brien: compromise: canary rule = `primary_region == us-west` (i.e. the incident’s owning region), not “contains”. if it becomes global, it’s no longer canary-enabled.

Devon Price: we have `incident.primary_region`. ok.

Rafael Mendes: +1. in global we’ll fall back to manual status updates until we’re confident.

Aisha Bello: i’ll tag canary incidents in metrics (label `bot_canary=true`) so we can compare.

DeployBot: Deploy scheduled: incident-bot `v2.43.0` to production @ 2024-07-09 10:00 PT. (Owner: Connor O'Brien)

Connor O'Brien: cool.
Action items:
- Devon: add explicit kill switch + confirm targeting rule uses `primary_region` (due EOD Thu)
- Christine: confirm us-west status components config lands in prod before Tuesday
- Aisha: baseline dashboard + canary KPI panels
- Rafael: SRE sign-off + oncall heads-up in #eng-oncall

Devon Price: :thumbsup: i’ll post here w/ the flag names + exact targeting JSON once it’s ready.

Christine Wong: will do. i’ll also update the runbook snippet for “if bot draft-sync is on, publish flow is via modal” so oncall isn’t surprised.

Rafael Mendes: i’ll ping Sean too; he’ll want to know we’re canarying and not auto-publishing.

Connor O'Brien: thanks all. let’s keep the canary tight and reversible.
